Odin × Godot

Box3D authoring and framework samples

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

For an offline, single-player game, Kit and Replay are optional: see examples/box3d_offline, where one script creates a Box3D world, steps it each physics frame and copies body poses onto ordinary Godot nodes.

Start with the shared authoring contract for World, Body, Sensor and six shape Resources. Character movement, queries and joints describe fixed-tick value state and all eight joint families. The editor workflow covers Inspector/gizmo tools, deterministic Mesh baking, owning artifacts and optional debug drawing.

Use the separate Kit and Replay sample instructions. Both use shared authored content and the same Box3D backend; each keeps its own Session, tick ownership, complete checkpoint and recovery APIs. The migration guide maps ordinary Godot physics scenes to those explicit contracts and lists supported operations and named failures.

The source API is box3d/authoring/API.md. Native ownership and identity are documented in box3d/README.md, and SDK code/data/accounting requirements in box3d/godot/README.md. Completed authoring, motion and editor reports retain actual commands, artifact hashes, prior failures and platform limits. Export Gate C is a separate milestone.
